alternatives.text: Pip the rabbit stands before the toy cabinet's bare front panel, one sticky note pinched between two fingers, already reaching to press it flat. The note clings to Pip's fingertip while the cabinet stays untouched. Pip peels it with the free hand and it splits into two notes, one stuck to each hand. Pip presses both palms to the cabinet; they spring back and double into four notes, now dotting Pip's wrists. Pip backs away, arms out, and the four notes split into eight across Pip's arms and face. Pip freezes, eyes wide above a note stuck to the muzzle, and watches the last split finish. Pip deliberately lowers both arms and stops struggling. The still note-covered face turns toward the mirror. Pip holds still, breathing, until a sneeze bursts out and scatters the notes onto the cabinet. Pip is relieved, but the cabinet remains messy.
alternatives.title: The One-Note Problem
alternatives.ending: Pip is relieved, but the cabinet remains messy.
alternatives.motivation: Pip wants to place a single sticky note flat on the cabinet's empty front panel.
weaknesses: The mirror turn still competes with the sneeze for the final seconds.
Thin-note contact on the face remains a precision risk.
The retreat-triggered split may read as accidental rather than causal without careful staging.
alternatives.progression: The note clings to Pip's fingertip while the cabinet stays untouched; peeling splits it into two, pressing doubles them to four, and backing away splits them to eight across Pip's arms and face.

Face partially occluded by a note during the realization beat.
Sneeze scatter requires many small notes to move believably in one burst.
proposedChanges: Open on the single-note placement attempt rather than mid-multiplication so the first visible promise is the rule itself.
Replace the door-edge push with a backward retreat that triggers the four-to-eight split, giving a clearer full-body silhouette.
Move the realization to a deliberate lowering of arms and a held still beat before the mirror turn, so the reversal is earned rather than rushed.
alternatives.openingVisualState: Pip the rabbit stands before the toy cabinet's bare front panel, one sticky note pinched between two fingers, already reaching to press it flat.

alternatives.text: Pip the rabbit presses a single sticky note toward the toy cabinet's empty front panel, and it clings to Pip's fingertip while the cabinet stays untouched. Pip shakes the hand; the note splits into two, one on each hand. Pip claps both hands onto the cabinet to transfer them, but they bounce back and double into four notes stuck across Pip's chest. Pip grabs at the four with both arms and they split into eight, wrapping Pip's arms and face. Pip sees the doubling finish and goes still, then slowly sits down on the floor, arms folded, refusing to touch anything. The notes stay put. Pip's nose twitches; a sneeze erupts and scatters the notes onto the cabinet. Pip is relieved, but the cabinet remains messy.
alternatives.title: Stop Trying
alternatives.ending: Pip is relieved, but the cabinet remains messy.
alternatives.motivation: Pip wants to transfer the sticky note onto the cabinet and be done with it.
weaknesses: Sitting down may read as giving up rather than realizing the rule.
The chest-stuck notes reduce face visibility for the sneeze.
Without a mirror, the realization is conveyed only by posture.
alternatives.progression: Shaking splits the note into two, clapping doubles them to four across Pip's chest, and grabbing splits them to eight over arms and face; Pip then sits down and refuses to touch anything.
